question:
(a) Define electric current and obtain the relation between current and charge flowing through a cross-section of a conductor.
(b) A charge of $60\,\text{C}$ flows through a conductor in $2\,\text{min}$. Calculate the current through the conductor.
(c) State whether electric current is a scalar or vector quantity and justify your answer.

options.A:
(a) Current is charge multiplied by time: $I=Qt$.
(b) $I=7200\,\text{A}$.
(c) Electric current is a vector because it has a direction.
options.B:
(a) Electric current is the rate of flow of charge: $I=\dfrac{\Delta Q}{\Delta t}$; for steady current, $I=\dfrac Qt$.
(b) $I=\dfrac{60}{120}=0.5\,\text{A}$.
(c) Current is a scalar quantity because it does not obey vector addition; currents at a junction add algebraically.
options.C:
(a) Current is time per unit charge: $I=\dfrac tQ$.
(b) $I=2\,\text{A}$.
(c) Current is a vector because electrons have velocity.
options.D:
(a) Current is charge per unit voltage: $I=\dfrac QV$.
(b) $I=60\,\text{A}$.
(c) Current is neither scalar nor vector.
